newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares soar 4.02 pct to new record.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares soar 4.02 pct to new record.

text.p: The IMKB National-100 index at the Istanbul's stock exchange surged 4.02 percent in lively trade on Friday to hit an all-time high close of 1,035.
It was up 40 points from the previous record of 995 on Thursday. Two-day gains totalled six percent after the market reopened following an extended new year holiday which began on December 27.
Trade volume leapt to 13.79 trillion lira from Thursday's 8.55 trillion.
Brokers said activity was led by shares of companies with bright 1996 profit prospects and largely state-owned firms due to refreshed privatisation hopes.

"The rise continued from yesterday, but was stronger. The market seems to have shaken off Thursday's cautious mood. Buying spilled over to the whole market and raised the chance of an upward trend for next week," said Ali Guler from Acar securities.
"The index neared the 97-cent medium-term target which may prompt some profit-taking. But selective activity will continue. Trends in alternative markets are also in favour of the bourse," he added.
In dollar terms, the index stood at 95.5 cents, up from 91 cents on December 27 and compared to a 1996 record of $1 on April 8.

Of the 233 shares traded, gainers outdid losers sharply by 150 to 36 and 47 closed stable. The IMKB Industrial index leapt 3.17 percent to 1,105, the IMKB Services surged five percent to 1,091 and the IMKB Financial jumped 3.75 percent to 969.

Actives were led by T.Isbank's C series shares, up 1,000 lira at 18,250, largely state owned flat steel giant Eregli which firmed 750 lira to 13,750 and utility Cukurova Elektrik, up 5,000 lira at 132,500. Together, they made up 16.5 percent of the total turnover.

The Exchange simplified the December 27 closing values of the composite, industrial and financial indices by dividing them by 100 and introduced several new indices to represent separate sectors, sub-sectors and markets from January 2.
